title: JsonUI attribute semantics — observable cross-platform contract
notes: Hand-authored canonical rulings (semantic-drift track 33, established 2026-08-03). Each adjudicated attribute-semantics ruling is declared ONCE here; the 'observable' block states the cross-platform effect expectation that `jui conformance gate --cross-effect` verifies mechanically against every platform's control-diff verdicts (expectation values: 'uniformly-inert' = the fixture must render identically to its control on every in-scope platform; 'uniformly-active' = it must differ on every in-scope platform). Toolchain code comments must POINT here instead of restating the rule — comment canon rots (the border ruling reversed direction twice within 48 hours while living as comments in three toolchains). Canonical choices are design decisions, not majority votes of existing implementations. Add one entry per ruling as the cross-effect adjudication queue is consumed.

border.ruling: A border is drawn only when BOTH borderWidth and borderColor are declared; borderWidth alone renders nothing on every platform — there is no default border color (2026-08-03 user ruling; supersedes the transient gray-default direction of d2c8628, unified across toolchains in 3e87b96). borderColor alone renders nothing for the same reason — the pair is what requests a border, and neither half requests one on its own (measured 2026-08-04, plan 34 re-measure: 0 px against the control on all three platforms; the android codegen does emit on the attribute's PRESENCE, which is a codegen-stage fact plan 41 tracks, not a rendered difference). borderStyle alone likewise renders nothing: it styles a border the width+color pair requests, it never summons one (2026-08-03 user ruling #2). NOTE: TextField.borderStyle is a DIFFERENT attribute (UIKit text-field chrome: roundedRect/line/bezel/none) and is outside this entry. The `__*_with_border` fixtures are the paired variants (borderStyle declared ALONGSIDE borderWidth + borderColor) that plan 49 added once three lanes had implemented the attribute with nothing measuring it — the lone-style fixtures above stay inert and keep testing the AND rule. `solid_with_border` is inert for a different reason from the lone ones: solid is the declared default of borderStyle, so stating it explicitly draws the same picture as omitting it (codegen_effect calls this class `value-is-default`). dashed/dotted are the two that must differ from the control. If the 3PF measurement comes back split rather than uniform, the honest record is a per-platform map like skinIdioms uses, not a forced uniform verdict: plan 34 caught ios emitting identical text for solid and dashed (C2/presence-only), and B/C/A implemented the three platforms separately in this wave. MEASURED 2026-08-05 (conformance-mobile run 30950551601 @ 5aada98), and the split the paragraph above anticipated is what happened: dashed and dotted are active on android and web and INERT on ios — the three borderStyle values render pixel-identical to each other and to the control on ios, which is the same symptom plan 34 recorded at the codegen stage (sjui emitting the same text for solid and dashed, C2/presence-only). They are therefore recorded as per-platform maps, not forced to a uniform verdict. This records today's reality; it does not bless it. If ios is supposed to draw a dashed border, the entry moves to uniformly-active once it does. solid_with_border stays uniformly-inert on all three because solid is borderStyle's declared default.

highlight.ruling: The highlighted appearance is drawn only when BOTH `highlighted` and a highlight colour are declared — the same pair-required shape as `border`, and ruled the same way. `highlighted: true` alone swaps the background to a colour that was never given, so nothing changes; `highlightBackground` alone names a colour for a state the view is never in. Every codegen already treats them as a pair (kjui modifier_builder.rb:490 combines highlight_cond with highlight_bg; sjui apply_highlighted_to_bag does the same), so a single-attribute fixture measures the absence of the companion rather than the converter. Established by measurement, not assumption: plan 41's paired probe carried View.highlighted as its one PROVISIONAL entry, and giving it `highlightBackground` made the ios/C0 and android/C0 findings disappear — the converters were correct and the fixture was missing the other half. This entry retires that PROVISIONAL: the pairing is now derived from the ledger like every other family (2026-08-05, plan 49-E, on plan 41's evidence). MEASURED 2026-08-05 (same run): web is active — A routed the highlight background through an inline style instead of a losing Tailwind class — while ios and android are still inert, so the verdict is recorded per platform. NOTE for anyone tidying this block: `common/highlightBackground__static` carries no control in the generated fixture set, so it is never compared and its verdict here is not checked against anything. It must NOT be deleted regardless — companions.py derives the pairing from this topic's `observable` KEYS, and a topic with fewer than two members stops producing companions at all.

image.ruling: 2026-08-03 user rulings: (a) the default contentMode is fit on every platform — web's implicit cover default was drift (fixed in rjui, 22d96b4); (b) fill is the stretch (scaleToFill synonym) — AspectFill is the crop. All three platforms now implement the full mapping including the positional modes (unscaled + aligned + cropped; sjui/kjui/SwiftJsonUI/KotlinJsonUI, 33 wave). Observables: fit-valued fixtures equal the default rendering (uniformly inert); fill/scaleToFill differ from it everywhere (uniformly active). Verified on the 33 round-3 measurement.

textView.flexibleHeight: declared height is the growth floor
textView.ruling: 2026-08-03 user ruling (31 handoff): with flexible enabled, the declared height is the floor the view GROWS from — it never shrinks below it to follow smaller content. android's behavior is canonical; ios (both paths) shrank with content and must adopt the floor formula min = minHeight ?? height ?? default (landed in the 33 wave: SwiftJsonUI dynamic + sjui codegen, floor formula min = minHeight ?? height). web measures 'has effect' — verify it matches floor semantics before recording it anywhere. No activeness observable: at fixture content size a correct floor renders identically to the control (that is WHY the android control_diff entry was removed in e78af64); the mechanical check belongs to the geometry probe (systematic-detection optimization track).

size.ruling: 2026-08-03 user ruling (31 handoff): matchParent + maxWidth/maxHeight resolves to min(parent extent, bound) — the bound clamps the fill. Generated code is canonical (kjui emits the constraint before the fill since 847fb56); KJUI dynamic ordered fillMaxWidth before widthIn, ignoring the bound entirely — reordered in the 33 wave (bounds precede a fill, stay after an explicit size). The composite clamp fixtures below are the observable: a clamping platform renders visibly narrower/shorter than its filled control (active); ignoring the bound renders identically (inert). Companion precedence (2026-08-03 campaign adjudication): an EXPLICIT numeric dimension pins the constraints and its bound stays inert (kjui codegen 847fb56, ios 35efc2b, rjui skips max-* under an explicit size); bounds in turn clamp a FILL. Order: explicit > bounds > fill.
size.explicitOverBounds: an explicit numeric dimension wins over its min/max bound

networkImage.ruling: 2026-08-03 user ruling: with no src, NetworkImage displays defaultImage; while loading it displays the first of hint/placeholder/loadingImage; on error it displays errorImage, falling back to defaultImage. Implemented on all platforms in the 33 wave (KotlinJsonUI defaultImage read + Coil fallback chain; ios placeholder no longer collapses over defaultImage; rjui defaultImage prop + template state machine). State-image fixtures use the DISTINCT conformance_sample_alt asset, so a hijacked no-src state renders visibly — the uniformly-inert observables verify the chain end-to-end. MEASURED 2026-08-05 (same run): placeholder is now active on all three — the conformance host never completes a network load, so the loading state persists and the placeholder is what the fixture shows; inert was the wrong expectation for it and the contract is updated. errorImage and loadingImage are active on android and inert on ios (they are out of scope on web), recorded per platform. OPEN QUESTION, deliberately not resolved by this entry: under the ruling above a state image should only appear in its own state, so android rendering a difference for errorImage — when the fixture never errors — reads like android showing a state image it should not, i.e. a defect rather than a contract. Recorded as measured because the gate cannot be satisfied by a ledger reason, but the android/ios split here needs adjudicating by the lanes that own those runtimes before it is treated as intended.

margins.offsetModel: ZStack/overlay child margins are full-margin offsets; an explicit center declaration disables that axis margin; margins arrays and start/endMargin apply as padding
margins.ruling: 2026-08-03 campaign adjudication (31/33 rounds, measured bbox evidence in the 33 geometry diagnosis table): an overlay (ZStack) child offsets by the FULL margin on each declared edge; declaring centerInParent/centerHorizontal/centerVertical disables the margin on the centered axis; the margins array and the RTL start/endMargin spellings resolve as padding-equivalent insets. Divergent rows are ledgered per-fixture with their measured deltas; the mechanical closure is the geometry probe (systematic-detection optimization track, de-scoped from the completion gate). No activeness observable: position deltas are invisible to fixture-vs-control activeness when every platform moves.

gravityDefaults.ruling: 2026-08-03 campaign adjudication: the default content gravity is top|start on every container (CollectionStack pins Top; SafeAreaView spacer layouts anchor start). A platform centering by default is the deviant. No activeness observable — default-vs-default renders identically; the geometry probe closes it mechanically.

shadow.ruling: 2026-08-03 campaign adjudication (31 wave, unified in 3e87b96/ca65fb6): the shadow string pipe format is exactly five fields (color|offsetX|offsetY|blur|opacity); any other count renders NOTHING on every platform — no partial parsing, no platform default. The conformance fixtures ship the valid five-field pipe; a malformed-count probe belongs to the validator, not the render layer.

gradient.ruling: 2026-08-03 campaign adjudication (31 gradient family): the default gradient direction is vertical (top to bottom) on every platform; an explicit "vertical" therefore equals the default rendering.

skinIdioms.demarcation: control chrome may differ per platform; the DIFFERENCE ITSELF is contract-pinned
skinIdioms.ruling: 2026-08-03 campaign adjudication: platform-owned control chrome is a legitimate difference, but only in its adjudicated SHAPE — the observable pins each accepted divergence as an expected-difference pattern, so both disappearing and mutating fail the gate. Members: Blur effectStyle (android material variants differ visibly, ios materials render alike on flat surfaces per the 31 saturation analysis, web CSS blur is single-variant), TextField.borderStyle (UIKit field chrome — each platform draws its own; web renders none for the UIKit-only bezel variants), TabView.showLabels (ios hides tab labels, android/web keep the labeled bar). The tabview glyph-source family is the codegen-side counterpart, pinned permanently in codegen_parity.json (2026-08-03 user ruling).

progressValue.undeclaredDefault: 0 (empty bar) on a determinate ProgressView; kjui renders indeterminate chrome when nothing is declared
progressValue.ruling: 2026-08-04 campaign adjudication (closing the last unreviewed cross-effect row): `progress` is the canonical determinate value attribute (declared 0..1 in attribute_definitions); `value` is the undeclared legacy runtime spelling every reader keeps as fallback, canonical-first. Undeclared progress must NOT default to a nonzero fill — ios (dynamic + sjui codegen) defaulted to 0.5, which made the control half-full and the progress:0.5 fixture measured inert; android (both paths) read only the legacy `value` and ignored the canonical attribute entirely. Fixed canonical-first on every path (SwiftJsonUI ProgressConverter, sjui progress_converter.rb, KotlinJsonUI DynamicProgressComponent, kjui progress_component.rb, rjui progress_converter.rb). The observable pins the repair: a half-full bar must differ from its undeclared control on every platform.

segmentLabelColors.roleModel: fontColor is the unselected label, selectedFontColor the selected one (falling back to fontColor), tintColor the SELECTED segment's accent — drawn as a background fill on ios/web and as the TabRow indicator on Compose
segmentLabelColors.ruling: 2026-08-04 orchestrator adjudication (38, consumer field report): a Segment whose selected background is a brand colour had no way to declare a readable label — web hardcoded the unselected label and treated fontColor as the SELECTED label's fallback, so the name and the role were twisted, and neither spelling was declared for Segment at all. fontColor and selectedFontColor are now declared for Segment on every platform (the IconLabel.selectedFontColor precedent) and carry the roles above: rjui emits the unselected class from fontColor, sjui writes both UISegmentedControl title attributes (.normal and .selected), kjui fills contentColor / selectedContentColor. The swift-only normalColor and selectedColor keep resolving behind the new spellings — they are in live consumer use — and selectedBackground was dropped instead of declared: tintColor already means the selected background and a second spelling for it earns nothing. No activeness observable: the fixtures would need a selected-vs-unselected pair to separate the two roles, which the current single-value shape cannot express.
segmentLabelColors.tintColorAlignment: 2026-08-04 orchestrator adjudication (42): android used to feed tintColor into the selected LABEL colour, so one declaration painted different things per platform — it now feeds the indicator, which is Compose's selected-state accent (its default is Configuration.Segment.defaultSelectedBackgroundColor). The rendering SHAPE stays platform-native: a filled segment on ios/web, a TabRow indicator on Compose; TabRow has no per-segment background and containerColor is the whole row. Measured before the change: of the two consumer screens declaring Segment colours, the only android one resolved its label colour from selectedColor (which precedes tintColor in the old chain), so no shipped screen changes colour — the missing accent simply appears. indicatorColor was an undeclared second spelling for the same slot and its read was dropped; normalColor / selectedColor became declared aliases of fontColor / selectedFontColor, so every converter reads canonical names only.

boundSize.unitModel: a bound size attribute carries a runtime number in layout units: dp on android, points on ios, px on web
boundSize.ruling: 2026-08-04 orchestrator adjudication (36, consumer field report): all six size attributes (width, height, minWidth, maxWidth, minHeight, maxHeight) declare "binding" in attribute_definitions, so a bound value MUST be honoured on every platform. kjui resolves it to `.height(data.v.dp)` (process_dimension) and sjui to `.frame(height: data.v)` (frame_helper is_binding?); rjui dropped it silently because the value reached the Tailwind arbitrary-value mapper, which returns '' for any string that is not a CSS unit — the declaration produced no class and no inline style, and jui build stayed warning-free. rjui now routes a bound dimension to the inline style as a px template literal, and treats it as an EXPLICIT size for the shrink and explicit-over-bounds rules above. No activeness observable: a bound fixture renders whatever the host viewmodel supplies, so fixture-vs-control cannot separate honouring from ignoring.

distribution.spacingWins: an explicit spacing pins the gap; distribution still governs size
distribution.ruling: 2026-08-05 (plan 49-E), raised by F/G and measured across all three toolchains. The vocabulary is UIStackView's, and its four values split into TWO KINDS that the current implementations conflate: `fill` and `fillEqually` distribute SIZE among the children, while `equalSpacing` and `equalCentering` distribute the FREE SPACE between them. fill = children grow to consume the axis, leaving no free space (proportional to their content size); fillEqually = every child gets the SAME size regardless of content; equalSpacing = equal gaps between adjacent children, with no leading or trailing gap; equalCentering = equal centre-to-centre distances. CONSEQUENCE, and this is the part every platform gets wrong today: the two size values are NOT an arrangement. They are `Modifier.weight(1f)` on each child in Compose, `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` (or equal weights) in SwiftUI, and `flex-1` in CSS — not Arrangement.* and not justify-content. Mapping `fill` to SpaceBetween/justify-between is precisely backwards: fill means there is no free space left to distribute. MEASURED STATE 2026-08-05 — all three disagree with the canon AND with each other, and each collapses a DIFFERENT pair of values into one output, so no fixture comparing two declared values can tell them apart: android (kjui container_component.rb:129-140) sends fillEqually and equalCentering both to Arrangement.SpaceEvenly; web (rjui view_converter.rb:184-195) sends the same pair both to justify-evenly; ios (sjui view_converter.rb:217,367,383) synthesises identical Spacer sets for equalSpacing and equalCentering, and gives fillEqually between-only spacers, which is space-between rather than equal sizes. `fill` emits nothing on ios (correct by accident) and a space-between arrangement on the other two (wrong). WHY NO GATE CAUGHT IT: --inert-complete asks whether a fixture differs from its CONTROL. Two declared values that both differ from the control but are identical to EACH OTHER pass that check, and android parity passes too because codegen and dynamic collapse them the same way. A value-vs-value comparison is the missing instrument — this is the 'both wrong in the same direction reads as green' shape. SPACING PRECEDENCE: `spacing` and `distribution` are not mutually exclusive and the current Compose behaviour (spacing != null wins outright, distribution never read) is wrong for the size values. An explicit `spacing` pins the GAP, so it overrides the gap that equalSpacing/equalCentering would compute; it says nothing about size, so fill/fillEqually still apply underneath it. Same shape as the size topic's explicit > bounds > fill ordering: the more specific declaration wins the axis it speaks about, and only that axis. No observable entries yet: the fixtures that would prove this need to compare two declared VALUES against each other rather than each against the control, which the current generator does not emit. That instrument is the follow-up this ruling asks for.
